cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says, “And the people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua…” (Judges 2:7). Joshua took over leading Israel after Moses died (Joshua 1:1-2). So picture a whole stretch of days with the people serving the LORD. I'd bake a double batch for a run like that.

The answer is elders. The text says the people served the LORD through the days of Joshua “…and of the elders who outlived him…” (Judges 2:7). The verse describes those elders as “…who had seen all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.” So the serving ran through the days of Joshua and those elders. Keep that in your back pocket, friends, because it matters in a few verses.

The answer is in the land of his own inheritance. They buried Joshua “…in the land of his inheritance, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.” (Judges 2:9). That's a very specific address, and I like that. The text tells us just where he was laid to rest.

The answer is that they did not know the LORD or His works. The text says “…another generation rose up who did not know the LORD or the works that He had done for Israel.” (Judges 2:10). Compare the elders, who “…had seen all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.” (Judges 2:7). Different generation, different knowing. I think that's a big gap to fall into.

The answer is False. The text says the Israelites “…did evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals.” (Judges 2:11). The elders served the LORD (Judges 2:7), but this generation did not. It was a sharp turn, friends, from what came before.

The answer is the gods of the peoples around them. The text says they “…followed after various gods of the peoples around them.” (Judges 2:12). Notice the word various, because it wasn't just one god. And this is in the same verse that reminds us the LORD brought their fathers out of Egypt.

The answer is that they can no longer resist them. The text says the LORD “…sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, whom they were no longer able to resist.” (Judges 2:14). Enemies were on every side, friends. Israel couldn't stand against them.

The answer is calamity. The text says, “Wherever Israel marched out, the hand of the LORD was against them to bring calamity…” (Judges 2:15). Calamity is the verse's own word. I think this is a heavy one to read.

The answer is True. The text says the hand of the LORD was against them to bring calamity, “…just as He had sworn to them.” (Judges 2:15). He had sworn it ahead of time. So this didn't come out of nowhere.

The answer is that they save Israel from the plunderers. The text says the LORD “…raised up judges, who saved them from the hands of those who plundered them.” (Judges 2:16). After the plundering, here comes the rescue. These judges are rescuers.
The answer is False. The text says Israel “…did not listen to their judges.” (Judges 2:17). They bowed down to other gods instead. That's the opposite of listening.

The answer is fathers. The text says they “…quickly turned from the way of their fathers, who had walked in obedience to the LORD’s commandments…” (Judges 2:17). The fathers had walked in obedience. This generation turned off that road fast.

The answer is True. The text says “…the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning under those who oppressed them and afflicted them.” (Judges 2:18). He heard the groaning. That's why the judges keep coming.

The answer is that they become even more corrupt than their fathers. The text says “…when the judge died, the Israelites became even more corrupt than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them.” (Judges 2:19). Once the judge was gone, they slid back. And they slid further than before.

The answer is that they broke His covenant and ignored His voice. The LORD says, “Because this nation has transgressed the covenant I laid down for their fathers and has not heeded My voice…” (Judges 2:20). Those are His own words about it. The covenant was crossed and His voice went unheeded.

The answer is nations. The LORD says, “I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.” (Judges 2:21). Nations were left standing when Joshua died. And the LORD says He won't drive them out now.

The answer is to test whether Israel will walk in His way. The LORD says, “In this way I will test whether Israel will keep the way of the LORD by walking in it as their fathers did.” (Judges 2:22). The reason is a test, in His own words, friends. He wants to see if they'll walk in His way.

The answer is warfare. The text says the nations were left “…if only to teach warfare to the subsequent generations of Israel, especially to those who had not known it formerly…” (Judges 3:2). Those younger folks hadn't known the wars in Canaan. This was about teaching them warfare.

The answer is that they marry into those peoples and serve their gods. The text says, “And they took the daughters of these people in marriage, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.” (Judges 3:6). Marriages going both ways, and then serving their gods. I think this one is a sad note to end on.
